key_insight: Optimized bi-stable nonlinear energy sinks passively redirect vortex-induced vibration energy in subsea cables into higher-frequency, more easily dissipated motions, reducing both vibration and drag.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a passive, retrofit-friendly way to improve subsea cable durability and fatigue life under realistic unsteady currents.
method: Integrated BNES attachments into the open-source MoorDyn cable model
Simulated fully 3D time-domain cable dynamics with Morison-type hydrodynamic forcing and varying currents
Used data-driven optimization across multiple current profiles to tune BNES parameters
evidence_signal: Across the sampled design space, well-tuned BNES configurations consistently reduced peak-to-peak vibration amplitudes, cumulative VIV energy intake, and drag energy.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful tuning and validation under broader load cases such as combined waves, platform motion, and long-term fatigue conditions.
paper_title: Bi-stable Nonlinear Energy Sinks (BNESs) for Response Mitigation and Drag Reduction of Subsea Cables Undergoing Vortex-induced Vibrations
